DATE : 11/10/2023 ORAL JUDGMENT :
1 Heard finally with the consent of learned Advocates for the parties.

2 This appeal and cross objection arises out of the judgment and award passed by the learned Ad-hoc District Judge-2, Washim (For short 'the Reference Court') dated 16.04.2012 and therefore,
the same are being disposed of by common judgment.

The Reference Court, by the impugned judgment and award, enhanced the compensation in respect of land from Rs.23,000/- per hector to Rs.89,500/- per acre and rejected the prayer for enhancement of compensation in respect of 35 Orange trees.
3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt 3 Background facts:
Respondent No.1- Dhanu Ratna Jadhav in the appeal is hereinafter referred to as 'the claimant'.
The land admeasuring 1.14 H.R. from Survey No. 129 situated at Mouza Waigaul, Tal Manora, District Washim was acquired for the purpose of Waigaul Dam Project.
The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act of 1894,) was published on 30.04.1998.
After completion of the required procedure the Special Land Acquisition Officer passed award on 16.12.2000.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.23,000/- per hector for the acquired land and Rs.7000/- for 35 Orange trees.

sentences.text: The claimant was not satisfied by this award.
Therefore, he filed reference application before the Collector and claimed enhancement in the compensation.
The Collector, forwarded the reference to the District Court, Washim.
3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt 5
Before the Reference Court, the appellant filed the written statement and opposed the claim.
It was contended that in the portion of the acquired land, only 35 Orange trees were planted.
The height of the Orange trees was around 0.85 meter.
The compensation, according to the appellant, awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer, was just, proper and reasonable.
It was contended that compensation claimed by the claimant was excessive and exorbitant.
6 The Reference Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.89,500/- per acre.
The Reference Court rejected the prayer for enhancement of compensation in respect of the Orange trees.
The State and acquiring body, being aggrieved by the enhancement of the compensation with regard to the land, has filed the appeal.
The claimant, being aggrieved by inadequacy of the compensation in respect of the land and rejection of reference with regard to the Orange trees, has filed cross-objection.
judge.odt 7
Heard learned Advocate for the appellant, learned Advocate for respondent No.1 and learned AGP for the State.
Perused the record and proceedings.
Following points fall for my determination.
i] Whether enhancement of the compensation in respect of the land granted by the Reference Court was just, proper and reasonable ?
ii] Whether the Reference Court was right in rejecting the enhancement of the compensation in respect of Orange trees ?
8 Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that compensation awarded in respect of the land at the rate of Rs.89,500/-/- per acre is just and reasonable.

Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that in respect of the similarly situated lands in First Appeal No. 581 of 2007 alongwith Cross objection No. 1 of 2008 (The State of Maharashtra and others .v/s. Harichand Bhasu Rathod,
3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt decided on 23.03.2016) the compensation awarded for the land was Rs.89,500/- per acre.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra and others .v/s. Harichand Bhasu Rathod
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that therefore the compensation awarded by the Reference Court is proper.
9 Learned Advocate for the claimant/respondent No.1 submitted that as far as the land is concerned the case of the claimant would be covered by the decision in First Appeal No. 581 of 2007.
Learned Advocate further submitted that the Reference Court rejected the claim for enhancement of compensation in respect of the Orange trees.

Learned Advocate, relying upon decision in First Appeal No. 509 of 2014 alongwith Cross objection No. 18 of 2017 (Narendra Tukaram Pawankar and Another .v/s. V.I.D.C., Washim, decided on 20.12.2018), submitted that the decision in First Appeal No. 581 of 2007 was made the basis to determine the value of the Orange trees.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate, therefore, submitted that in this case the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer at the rate of Rs.200/- per Orange tree is not reasonable and it is required to be enhanced.

10 Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the joint measurement report relied upon by the claimant indicates that there were 35 Orange trees and the height of the trees was hardly 0.85 meter.
Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the Reference Court therefore rightly rejected the report of the valuer Exh. 38, wherein the value of each Orange tree was shown as Rs.2000/-.

Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that in the earlier decisions relied upon by the claimant, the relief was granted by inadvertence or mistake and therefore, the same will not create legal right in favour of respondent No.1 to claim the compensation.
In order to support this submission he has relied upon the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Basawaraj and 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt
Another .v/s.
Special
Land Acquisition Officer 1.

In this case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that if the wrong or illegality or irregularity had been committed in earlier proceedings, then similarly situated persons cannot invoke jurisdiction of Courts for repeating or multiplying such illegality.
11 As far as the agricultural land is concerned, the issue has been settled in view of the above decisions in the above First Appeals.

As far as the Orange trees are concerned,
though the claimant has stated that there were 277 Orange trees, the evidence on record is not sufficient to accept this contention.
It is seen that 277 trees were planted in the entire land admeasuring 2.34 H.R.
At the time of joint measurement, only 35 Orange trees were found planted in the land admeasuring 1.14 HR.
The valuer, in his report, has stated that trees were 5 to 6 years old and started bearing the fruits.

Joint Measurement Report report shows that the trees were 1 (2013)
14 SCC 81 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt having height of 0.85 meters.
In my view, therefore the claimant has failed to establish that he is entitled for parity with the claimants in the above appeals.
It is seen that in the above appeals the Orange trees were around 10-12 years old, for which the compensation awarded for per Orange tree was at the rate of Rs.4000/-.
Therefore, the learned Advocate for the appellant was right in placing reliance on the decision in the case of Basawaraj and Another .v/s. Special Land Acquisition Officer (supra) .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In my view, the Reference Court was not right in maintaining the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer in respect of the Orange trees at the rate of Rs.200/- per tree.

Even if it is assumed that the height of the trees was 0.85 meters and the age of the trees was 5-6 years, the Reference Court ought to have taken into consideration all surrounding facts and circumstances.
The Reference Court has not considered even the costs that might have been incurred by the claimant for maintaining the trees 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt for 5-6 years.
The valuer in his report has stated that the value of the Orange trees was Rs.2000/- per tree.
The Reference Court has not properly appreciated the evidence.
In the facts and circumstances even by doing some guess work the Reference Court ought to have awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.1000/- per tree in respect of 35 Orange trees.

In my view,
therefore, in this case the compensation for the 35 Orange trees is required to be enhanced to Rs.1000/- per tree.
The compensation already awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is required to be deducted from this amount.
The claimant, therefore, would be entitled to get interest

sentences.text: 12 Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the Reference Court has granted the interest under Section 28 of the Act of 1894 from the date of taking possession.

Learned Advocate, relying upon a decision of the Full Bench of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra .v/s. Kailash Shiva 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt Rangari2, submitted that the claimant would be entitled to get interest from the date of the award at the rate of 9% p.a. for first year and thereafter at the rate of 15% p.a. till realization of the entire amount of compensation.

In the case of State of Maharashtra .vs/. Kailash (supra) it is held that if the possession of land under acquisition is taken before the notification under Section 4(1) of the Act of 1894 is published and/or before the award is passed, the land owner would be entitled for interest as per Section 34 necessarily from the date of passing of the award under Section 11 of the said Act, except in cases where the possession is taken in accordance with Section 17 of the said Act, and in that situation only, the provision of Section 34 of the said Act shall start operating from the date of possession.

In this case, therefore, the claimant would be entitled to get interest from the date of the award under Section 28 of the Act of 1894 at the rate of 9% p.a. for the first year and thereafter at the rate of 15 % p.a. 2 2016 (3) Mh.L.J. 457 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt Clause (5) of the impugned judgment and order is, therefore, required to be modified.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative and point No. 2 in the negative.
13 The First appeal stands dismissed.
The cross objection is partly allowed.

14 The impugned judgment and order passed by the Reference Court, dated 16.04.2012, awarding compensation at the rate of Rs.89,500/- per acre for acquisition of 1.14 H.R. land out of Survey No.
129, is maintained.
It is set aside to the extent of rejection of enhancement of compensation for Orange trees.
15 The compensation for Orange trees is enhanced.

The claimant is entitled to receive the compensation at the rate of Rs.1000/- per tree in respect of 35 Orange trees.
3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt 16

If the claimant has already received the amount of compensation, then on the balance outstanding the claimant would be entitled to receive interest at the rate of 9 % per annum under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for the period of one year from the date of award and for the period thereafter @ of 15 % per annum till full realization of the amount.
17 The other statutory entitlements, as are granted by the Reference Court, shall remain intact.
18 The appellant is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within twelve weeks.
19 The amount already deposited by the appellant be deducted from the enhanced amount of compensation.
20 The claimant/respondent No.1 shall be permitted 3.fa.262.2015 judge.odt to withdraw the entire amount of compensation alongwith interest, if any accrued thereon.
21 The appeal and cross objection stand disposed of accordingly.
No order as to costs.
